what_it_does: Understanding why a GPU program is slow requires knowing where the GPU's computing units are spending idle time — waiting for memory, waiting for a synchronization barrier, or waiting for the next instruction. Existing profiling tools assign each idle cycle to a single highest-priority cause, which misrepresents situations where multiple stalls are overlapping and hides the true bottleneck. GCStack is a richer cycle-accounting method that records all simultaneously active stall types for every cycle, producing a more accurate picture. GCScaler then takes that one-time measurement and uses analytical scaling formulas to predict how performance would change if you modified the GPU's design — adjusting memory bandwidth, number of cores, cache sizes — without running the simulation again. The abstract claims this lets engineers evaluate 1,000 GPU design variants from a single simulation run.
